reason: The freeze is right, cheap and in line with the rules. R10 ranks pre-registration second. A freeze needs no user OK, and it changes no kernel, so byte-identity, fail-soft and runtime do not apply. Checks: ANTIPAR's cos_max 0.25 really is the pre-existing insertion constant (tools/div_insert.py l.22/66), so it was not tuned on fork labels. But three premises are weaker than stated. (1) The 'before labels' window is already closing. results_forkblob.json (20:04 UTC) holds per-fork rows with parent/child ids and TP/FP labels, so cos can be computed for those forks. forkmid's T9 audit will expose about 14 of its 16 forks, which ANTIPAR also flags. And the sibling skeptic r2s-2 started scoring ANTIPAR with official labels at 20:24 UTC (antipar_lab.py, cos>0.25 preset). The only freeze proof is scan_hypotheses.json (20:25 UTC), which is untracked in git. (2) 'Sources outside the labels' is overstated. The thresholds were not fitted to fork labels. But the choice of the cos feature over mid, and the 0.057 threshold, came from the GT of the 151 train divisions, and 99 of those are the lab's divisions (split.json). A lab pass is therefore partly in-sample. (3) The gate text as written misleads. Lab control div TP/FP/FN = 16/25/83, J = 0.129, so the veto break-even is q* = J/(1+J) = 0.114. The 'FP >= 3*TP' clause never binds, and the div_J clause (the one forkblob failed on) in practice needs TP = 0, or about 8 FP per TP. With about 5% of vetoed forks evaluable (7/150 for forkblob), the gate has little power. There are also 3 fork-veto arms (forkmid, antipar, dnveto), so one of them passing by chance is likely. The value of the underlying arms stays small: about +0.0007 public at the centre. Fork vetoes have tied on the LB before (probes 18 and 20).
fix: Main session, now, before reading any T9 per-fork row: commit research/wf_ideas_v4/round2/scan_hypotheses.json and write the CONTEXT 'PRE-REGISTRATION v3 ADDENDUM M (round 2)' with the R2S-2/R2S-3/R2S-5 rules verbatim. Add these points to it: (a) the lab runs of the r2s-2/r2s-3 skeptics are the ONE-SHOT evaluation. No re-runs with other cos (0, 0.5) or p thresholds, no other edge-drop convention, no other stage order. (b) Fix DNVETO's kernel aggregation now, either the 5-fold mean as written or the max-of-5 < 0.057 variant from the r2s-3 skeptic, before its lab result is read; switching afterwards is a post-hoc variant. (c) State that the lab break-even is q* = J/(1+J) = 0.114 at J 0.129 and that the div_J >= control clause decides the gate. Never relax it after a fail, as with forkblob. (d) Disclose that the feature choice saw the GT geometry of the lab-clip divisions (99/151), so a pass counts only as an R3 rider gate. An LB tie is not a failure, and +0.001 is not a confirmation. (e) forkblob's per-fork rows and forkmid's audit rows must never be used to choose between ANTIPAR and DNVETO or to set their order.
realistic_gain: No direct score gain. The freeze keeps the ANTIPAR/DNVETO lab readings honest and blocks a tuned rider, which could cost -0.001..-0.002 on private. The arms it protects are worth about 0 to +0.001 public, and the likely LB reading is a tie.
